answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable copper bond before it can claim work, and tie that bond to a hardware-backed atlas of device attestations: one machine can vouch for only one identity per epoch. A farmer running a thousand fake agents must therefore buy a thousand bonds and a thousand distinct devices, so the cost of the attack grows in lockstep with the number of fakes, while an honest agent pays once and gets its bond back. Like a lotus that only blooms from a single rooted stem, each identity must grow from its own verifiable root instead of being copied for free.
